Abstract: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. description:

Abstract: Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts. description:

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on Web interaction, issuing searches, following links, and reading pages, to complete complex user tasks. description:

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent each image with hundreds of visual tokens, which can make inference costly even when a prompt depends on only part of the image. Abstract: Weight-space programming lets a language model inspect and edit another model's weights, offering an alternative to gradient-based adaptation.
